_doc: Registry of factual claims used in the library, each paired with a public source.
Every numeric or specific factual claim in an article should either:
(a) appear here with a source URL, or
(b) be labeled illustrative/directional in the prose itself, or
(c) be sourced inline via a <details class="cite">…</details> drawer.
If a claim doesn't fit one of those three patterns, it doesn't belong in the library.
When in doubt, cut. When the source is private (operator experience), label it as such.
claim:       the factual assertion as written
source_url:  primary public URL (vendor pricing page, search-industry analysis, Google docs, etc.)
date_verified: YYYY-MM-DD when last checked against the source
used_in:     list of article slugs (or page paths) that cite this claim
notes:       what to watch for if the source changes

gpo_independent_savings_2026.claim: Independent restaurants commonly report saving roughly 10–30% on food and supply costs by buying through a group purchasing organization, which aggregates volume to reach pricing tiers a single operator buying direct from a distributor cannot.
gpo_independent_savings_2026.notes: 10–30% savings range cross-checked across Restaurant Business (GPO 101 / Dining Alliance, Foodbuy), FoodIndustry.com, and SevenRooms (snippet-verified; full fetches 403-blocked). Directional leverage figure used in the Fair-Price Gap 'worth asking' copy — it frames the upside of negotiating/aggregating when a paid price sits far above the wholesale reference, not a guaranteed saving.

usda_wholesale_protein_oil_refs_2026.claim: USDA/CME wholesale reference levels (2026): boxed ribeye ~$10.71/lb and tenderloin ~$15.91/lb (grass-fed whole tenderloin $25–44/lb); ground beef 81/85% lean ~$3.91–4.41/lb; short ribs ~$8–10.5/lb; boneless skinless chicken breast ~$1.14–1.97/lb; CME soybean oil ~$0.48/lb (bulk ~$0.50–1.20/lb).
usda_wholesale_protein_oil_refs_2026.source_name: USDA AMS National Weekly Boxed Beef Cutout; CME soybean oil
usda_wholesale_protein_oil_refs_2026.notes: Snippet-verified across USDA AMS boxed-beef reports (ams.usda.gov/mnreports), beefitswhatsfordinner wholesale update, IndexBox (2026-03-16), USDA pork summary, and CME soybean oil (2026-06-12); several full fetches 403-blocked. Used ONLY to ground the Cost Index data-quality audit's plausibility bands and reference deviations — directional wholesale references, not delivered prices. Re-check against the live USDA/CME reports before any hard figure lands in prose.

food_cost_target_band_2026.claim: The long-standing industry target for restaurant food cost is 28–35% of food sales, and it varies by service model: quick-service / fast-casual roughly 25–30%, casual ~30–34%, and fine dining ~34–40% (premium ingredients, lower covers).
food_cost_target_band_2026.source_name: Restaurant365 — What is a good food cost percentage?
food_cost_target_band_2026.notes: 28–35% band and service-model breakdown cross-checked across Restaurant365, NetSuite restaurant benchmarks, getmeez, and ChowNow (snippet-verified; full fetch blocked 403). Grounds the default food-cost target in tools/_shared/plate-market-recost.js. Segment edges are approximate industry ranges, not one authority's exact figure — keep labeled as a band.

protein_highest_cost_category_2026.claim: Protein is typically the highest-cost ingredient category on a restaurant menu, and protein price volatility is a primary driver of food-cost-percentage swings.
protein_highest_cost_category_2026.source_name: meez — How to calculate food cost
protein_highest_cost_category_2026.notes: Snippet-verified across meez and ChowNow (full fetch blocked 403). Directional industry claim; supports prioritizing protein lines in the cost-pressure and market-recost surfaces.

menu_price_lag_wholesale_2025.claim: Menus lag supplier costs: U.S. full-service menu prices rose about 4.4% year-over-year as of mid-2025, while wholesale food costs remained far above pre-pandemic levels (the source cites 36%+).
menu_price_lag_wholesale_2025.notes: Snippet-verified (full fetch blocked 403). The ~4.4% YoY menu figure aligns with the BLS 'food away from home' CPI trend; the 36%+ wholesale-vs-pre-pandemic figure is Barmetrix's compilation. Re-check against BLS CPI/PPI before any hard number lands in prose; treat as directional. This gap is the core motivation for automatic market recost.

menu_recost_cadence_six_months_2026.claim: Operators are advised to revisit menu pricing in smaller increments roughly every six months rather than infrequent large jumps, because a dish costed six months earlier may have drifted significantly as supplier prices move.
menu_recost_cadence_six_months_2026.notes: Snippet-verified across GoFoodService and MarketMan recipe-costing guidance (full fetch blocked 403). Grounds the recost capability's value proposition: automatic market recost vs the existing 'quarterly check-in' manual banner.

google_core_update_may_2026.claim: Google's May 2026 core update began rolling out on May 21, 2026 and may take up to two weeks to complete; it is the second core update of the year.
google_core_update_may_2026.notes: Google Search Status Dashboard (status page; tld-only). 'Up to two weeks' is Google's estimate, not a confirmed end date.

rio_seo_restaurant_decline_2026.claim: A 2026 local-search analysis found restaurant Google Maps views down 40.1% and food orders from those listings down 25.7% over two years, even as rankings held.
rio_seo_restaurant_decline_2026.notes: Rio SEO 2026 report (snippet-verified; full fetch blocked). Restaurant-specific engagement declines; treat as their measured figures.

sterling_sky_ai_local_pack_2026.claim: AI local packs appeared on roughly 7% of tracked local keywords in 2026 and dropped the click-to-call button when shown.
sterling_sky_ai_local_pack_2026.source_name: Sterling Sky — The State of Local SEO in 2026
sterling_sky_ai_local_pack_2026.notes: Sterling Sky 2026 (snippet-verified). ~7% of tracked keywords; AI local packs drop click-to-call. The circulated '68% of local queries' figure is a service-industry stat and was NOT used for restaurants. Zero-click stated directionally ('the majority'), not as a hard percentage.

brightedge_gemini_referral_2026.claim: Gemini became the #2 AI referral source in 2026, rising from 4.3% to 11.6% of AI referrals in Q1 and 13.2% by April, while ChatGPT fell from 89.2% to 81.4%.
brightedge_gemini_referral_2026.notes: BrightEdge release May 20, 2026 (snippet-verified; exact press-release slug not confirmed, so registered at the press hub as tld-only). '~13%' is the April figure; Q1 share is 11.6%. Both stated to avoid conflation.

google_ai_mode_io_2026.claim: At Google I/O on May 19, 2026, Google rebuilt AI Mode on a new model with a redesigned search box and agentic capabilities, including booking restaurant tables through OpenTable, Resy, and Tock; AI Mode reaches 1B+ monthly users with US rollout over summer 2026.
google_ai_mode_io_2026.source_name: Google — The Keyword, I/O 2026 Search updates
google_ai_mode_io_2026.notes: Primary source is Google's own I/O recap (free host). Capabilities named by Google; specific per-query SERP layouts intentionally not asserted (a 'three categorized sections' layout circulating in recaps is NOT in the primary and was not used).

opentable_direct_booking_pref_2026.claim: 65% of diners prefer to book directly on a restaurant's own website rather than through a third party (OpenTable, 2026).
opentable_direct_booking_pref_2026.notes: OpenTable 2026 diner-trends figure (snippet-verified; full fetch blocked). Earlier-circulating 86%/45%/20->29% stats were NOT supported by this report and were dropped.

uberall_ai_invisibility_2026.claim: A 2026 Uberall study found 83% of restaurants do not appear in AI search results, despite 86% having a Google Business Profile; AI assistants name only 3-5 brands per query.
uberall_ai_invisibility_2026.source_name: Uberall — Fast Food, Faster Discovery: The 2026 GEO Playbook for Multi-Location QSRs
uberall_ai_invisibility_2026.notes: QSR/multi-location study. Figures cross-checked across search snippets (BusinessWire, CityAM); full-page fetch was blocked, so treat exact percentages as Uberall's reported figures. Framed as QSR data generalized to independents, not an independents-only measurement.

uberall_ai_rating_floors_2026.claim: AI assistants apply minimum star-rating thresholds before recommending a restaurant: roughly 4.3 for ChatGPT, 4.1 for Perplexity, and 3.9 for Gemini (Uberall, 2026).
uberall_ai_rating_floors_2026.notes: Per-assistant rating floors are Uberall's reported figures, snippet-verified (WebFetch blocked). State as published ranges, not guaranteed cutoffs; assistants reweight often.

ai_overview_share_march_2025.claim: Google AI Overviews appeared on 13.14% of US desktop queries in March 2025
ai_overview_share_march_2025.notes: Search Engine Land, "Google AI Overviews now show on 13% of searches: Study" (article ID 455057). Verified via search 2026-05-14. The 13.14% figure is the most-cited measurement of AI Overview prevalence on US desktop search. Post-March-2025 trajectory is reported qualitatively across industry coverage; treat direction as "rising, not flat" until a comparable consolidated measurement is published.

doordash_marketplace_tiers.claim: DoorDash Marketplace commission tiers: Basic 15%, Plus 25%, Premier 30%
doordash_marketplace_tiers.notes: DoorDash Merchant pricing page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. The three Marketplace tiers (Basic 15%, Plus 25%, Premier 30%) are documented here; pickup commission is reduced to 6% across all tiers. Re-check quarterly because DoorDash renames tiers periodically.

uber_eats_published_rates.claim: Uber Eats commission tiers and Pro membership cost
uber_eats_published_rates.notes: Uber Eats Merchant pricing page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Updated marketplace fee structure (effective March 11, 2026): 30% Uber-delivery / 15% self-delivery / 7-10% pickup.

grubhub_published_rates.claim: Grubhub commission tiers and second-layer fee structure
grubhub_published_rates.notes: Grubhub merchant pricing-and-fees page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Marketing commission 5-20% depending on plan; order-processing 3.05% + $0.30; delivery 10% on Grubhub-delivered orders.

toast_rewards_pricing.claim: Toast Loyalty add-on monthly cost (~$50/month per Toast)
toast_rewards_pricing.notes: Toast Loyalty product page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Pricing: $50/month as an add-on to the core Toast POS platform.

square_loyalty_pricing.claim: Square Loyalty monthly cost (starts $25/month per Square)
square_loyalty_pricing.notes: Square Loyalty pricing help article. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Starting pricing $25/month per location; 30-day free trial available.

fivestars_pricing.claim: Fivestars standalone loyalty platform — no openly published pricing
fivestars_pricing.notes: Fivestars does NOT publish open monthly pricing. The platform is contact-for-quote. Any specific dollar range in operator-facing content must be labeled as operator-reported rather than vendor-published.

como_pricing.claim: Como standalone loyalty platform — no openly published pricing
como_pricing.notes: Como does NOT publish open monthly pricing. The platform is contact-for-quote. Same posture as Fivestars: any specific dollar range must be labeled operator-reported.

mailchimp_pricing.notes: Mailchimp marketing-plan pricing page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Free tier under 250 contacts; Essentials/Standard/Premium paid tiers scale with contact count.

klaviyo_pricing.notes: Klaviyo pricing page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Free under 250 profiles / 500 monthly sends; paid pricing starts at ~$30/month at the 500-1000 active-profiles tier.

google_local_ranking_signals.claim: Google ranks local results by distance, relevance, and prominence — and review-response activity is one of the signals weighted toward prominence
google_local_ranking_signals.source_name: Google Business Profile Help — Improve your local ranking
google_local_ranking_signals.notes: Google Business Profile Help — "Improve your local ranking." Stable Google support answer ID; URL has been live for years.

google_business_profile_help_photos.claim: Google states that businesses with photos receive significantly more directions requests and click-throughs than businesses without
google_business_profile_help_photos.source_name: Google Business Profile Help — Add photos and videos
google_business_profile_help_photos.notes: Google Business Profile Help — "Add photos and videos to your Business Profile." Stable answer ID. Google has cited specific percentages (42% more directions, 35% more click-throughs) in this documentation; the exact figures shift over time, the directional finding is consistent.

google_schema_supported_types.claim: Google Search Central documents Restaurant, Menu, OpeningHoursSpecification, AggregateRating, Reservation, and FAQPage as supported schema types for restaurant pages
google_schema_supported_types.source_name: Google Search Central — Local Business structured data
google_schema_supported_types.notes: Google Search Central — Local Business structured data. Stable Google docs URL.

dc_initiative_82.claim: DC Initiative 82 (Tipped Wage Workers Fairness Act) phases out the tipped minimum wage in the District of Columbia
dc_initiative_82.source_name: DC Office of Human Rights — Tipped Wage Workers Fairness Act
dc_initiative_82.notes: DC Office of Human Rights page on the Tipped Wage Workers Fairness Act. Verified via search 2026-05-14. The library previously cited a URL on does.dc.gov that did not exist — the canonical agency page for TWWFA is on OHR, not DOES. Initiative 82 itself was passed November 2022; tipped minimum wage increases annually until 2027 when it equals the full minimum wage.

instagram_2024_algorithm_update.claim: Meta's late-2024 algorithm update penalizes stacked-hashtag posts
instagram_2024_algorithm_update.notes: Meta's creator-blog announcements describe the 2024 algorithm change that penalized stacked-hashtag posts; specific percent-penalty figures are not published. Treat the directional effect as cited, the magnitude as qualitative. TLD-only link because the specific blog-post URL was not verified.

nielsen_norman_group_reference.claim: Nielsen Norman Group has published research on Fitts's Law and broader web usability
nielsen_norman_group_reference.source_name: Nielsen Norman Group — "Fitts's Law and Its Applications in UX"
nielsen_norman_group_reference.notes: NNG canonical Fitts's Law article. Verified via search 2026-05-14. The library previously linked to /articles/fittss-law/ (double-S) which 404'd — the canonical slug is /articles/fitts-law/ (single S). For non-Fitts NNG references (e.g. local-business usability), the library now credits NNG as a source-on-the-topic with a TLD or topic-page link rather than fabricating a specific article slug.

baymard_institute_reference.claim: Baymard Institute publishes a meta-analysis of cart-abandonment rate statistics
baymard_institute_reference.source_name: Baymard Institute — "50 Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics 2026"
baymard_institute_reference.notes: Baymard canonical cart-abandonment list. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Current average rate ~70.22% based on 50 studies. URL was correct in the library's original citation; the previous defensive sweep that degraded it to a TLD-only link has been reversed.

think_with_google_mobile_speed.claim: Think with Google has published research on mobile page-speed industry benchmarks
think_with_google_mobile_speed.source_name: Think with Google — "New Industry Benchmarks for Mobile Page Speed" (Daniel An, Feb 2017)
think_with_google_mobile_speed.notes: Think with Google canonical page on mobile page-speed benchmarks. Verified via search 2026-05-14. Source of the "53% of mobile site visitors leave a page that takes longer than three seconds to load" stat. URL was correct in the library's original citation.

national_restaurant_association_reports.claim: The National Restaurant Association publishes annual State of the Industry research
national_restaurant_association_reports.notes: NRA research-reports landing page. Verified via search 2026-05-14. 2026 State of the Industry projects industry sales ~$1.55T; ~100,000 jobs added; total employment 15.8M. URL was correct in the library's original citation.

cpi_food_away_from_home_may_2026.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI for May 2026 (released June 10, 2026)

cpi_food_at_home_may_2026.claim: Over the 12 months ending May 2026, the U.S. CPI food-at-home index rose 2.7% and the all-food index rose 3.1%.
cpi_food_at_home_may_2026.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI for May 2026 (released June 10, 2026)

usda_beef_veal_forecast_2026.claim: USDA ERS forecasts 2026 retail beef and veal prices up 12.1% (prediction interval 6.6 to 18.1%), the largest food-category increase, citing a U.S. cattle herd shrinking since 2019 against strong demand.
usda_beef_veal_forecast_2026.source_name: USDA Economic Research Service, Food Price Outlook (May 2026 forecast)
usda_beef_veal_forecast_2026.notes: Midpoint forecast; range is the 95% prediction interval.

usda_eggs_forecast_2026.claim: USDA ERS forecasts 2026 retail egg prices down 29.8% (prediction interval -38.8 to -18.3%) as the laying flock recovers from the HPAI avian-flu outbreak.
usda_eggs_forecast_2026.source_name: USDA Economic Research Service, Food Price Outlook (May 2026 forecast)
usda_eggs_forecast_2026.notes: Retail price forecast; distinct from farm-level PPI (-81.6%) and the April retail YoY (-39.2%). Measures kept separate.

usda_allfood_forecast_2026.claim: USDA ERS forecasts 2026 all-food prices up 3.4%, food away from home up 3.5%, and food at home up 3.2%.
usda_allfood_forecast_2026.source_name: USDA Economic Research Service, Food Price Outlook (May 2026 forecast)

muntin_cost_index_ribeye_2026_06.claim: The Muntin Cost Index put wholesale ribeye near $11.59 per pound as of June 5, 2026 (sourced from USDA Livestock Mandatory Reporting), flagged flat within its normal weekly range despite an upward two-year trend.
muntin_cost_index_ribeye_2026_06.source_name: Muntin Cost Index (data/cost-index.json, generated from verified sources only)
muntin_cost_index_ribeye_2026_06.notes: In-repo fact-gated value; provenance usda-lmr, asOf 2026-06-05, weekly flag verdict 'flat'.

fathers_day_2026_date.claim: Father's Day 2026 falls on Sunday, June 21 (the third Sunday in June).
fathers_day_2026_date.source_name: U.S. calendar (third Sunday in June); corroborated by OpenTable Father's Day 2026 listings.

nra_fathers_day_dining.claim: The National Restaurant Association's research ranks Father's Day among the most popular holidays for dining out (after Mother's Day and Valentine's Day).
nra_fathers_day_dining.source_name: National Restaurant Association — consumer dining research.
nra_fathers_day_dining.notes: Qualitative ranking from NRA research; no specific volume cited in the post.

opentable_fathers_day_reservations.claim: Restaurant reservations for Father's Day rise year over year, per OpenTable.
opentable_fathers_day_reservations.notes: Directional trend; the post states no specific percentage.

Operators who join the founding list before launch get the founding rate: three months free, then $19 a month per location for as long as they stay. Pricing is posted in writing at ledger.muntin.digital.
ledger_founding_offer_2026.source_name: Muntin Ledger — posted pricing (first-party, founder-confirmed 2026-06-27; per-location basis founder-confirmed 2026-07-09)

_doc: Claims that come from Don's restaurant-floor experience rather than a public source.
These ARE allowed in articles, but must be framed as operator practice — not as measured data.
If a claim says 'in operator practice' / 'we typically see' / 'restaurants we audit' it goes here.
If a claim says '42% of our diagnostics' / '600 reviews across two restaurants' it does NOT — it's pretending to be measurement and must come out.
operator_experience_claims.current_role: Full-time Front-of-House Manager at Tacombi in Bethesda, MD and Arlington, VA (Aug 2024 onwards). Tacombi is one restaurant brand; these are two of its locations, not two restaurants.
past_roles: Manager at The Irish Inn at Glen Echo (Aug 2024 – 2026)
Front-of-House Manager at Tacombi, Bethesda (Aug 2023 – Jul 2024) — first run
Floor Manager and Server at Kapnos Kouzina, Bethesda (Dec 2016 – Dec 2018)
